title: Planning a biology application? Start with three questions
hook: You do not need a highly specific research label on day one.
body:
You do not need a highly specific research label on day one.

If you are organizing ideas for a biology-related application, try writing down:
1. What research question interests you?
2. Which experience best explains that interest?
3. What would help next: research exposure, methods training, or better information?

This is a starting point for a conversation, not an admissions assessment. Our fictional research preparation Q&A has no confirmed date or participation arrangements.
cta: Organize your questions first, then decide whether a further conversation would help.
review_note: Fictional event example. Confirm event details and content ownership before any real use; do not invent speakers, institutions or outcomes.

title: From biology to bioinformatics: interests before a tool list
hook: Do you need to finish every programming course first? Start with a smaller question.
body:
Do you need to finish every programming course first? Start with a smaller question.

Which biological problems interest you? What data or research tasks have you already encountered? Which part of the analysis process feels unclear?

A one-page summary can make a discussion with classmates or a consulting colleague more useful than a list of tools. This example does not prescribe a course sequence or assess application competitiveness.
cta: Try a one-page question list as a starting point for your next conversation.
review_note: Editorial concept, not academic or admissions advice. Check audience relevance and natural tone.

audience: Prospective attendees of a research Q&A
title: What should you prepare before a research Q&A?
hook: You do not need a perfect application story to start a conversation.
body:
You do not need a perfect application story to start a conversation.

Bring three specific questions: What have I done so far? Where am I most uncertain? What would I like to test next?

If background information is relevant, prepare a short version without contact details. Event topics, times and speaker information must come from an approved announcement. This example demonstrates content planning only.
cta: Write down the one question you most want to ask.
review_note: No actual speaker or event is represented. Verify all factual claims and public release permission.
